name: Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type III

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic criteria for Congenital Dyserythropoietic Anemia Type III

criteria.description: Presence of giant multinucleated erythroblasts in bone marrow aspirate
Identification of pathogenic mutations in the KIF23 gene
Evidence of ineffective erythropoiesis on bone marrow examination
Elevated lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and indirect hyperbilirubinemia

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of giant multinucleated erythroblasts in bone marrow, macrocytic anemia, and pathogenic KIF23 mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is confirmed by bone marrow morphology combined with genetic testing.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Giant multinucleated erythroblasts in bone marrow
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic morphological finding on bone marrow biopsy

rare.symptomName: Cardiac complications secondary to chronic anemia
Iron overload due to repeated transfusions
Neurological symptoms related to severe anemia

laboratory: Macrocytic anemia with low reticulocyte count
Normal to low serum iron and ferritin unless transfused
other: Bone marrow biopsy showing giant multinucleated erythroblasts and ineffective erythropoiesis

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of binucleated erythroblasts rather than giant multinucleated forms
Mutations in CDAN1 or C15orf41 genes
Presence of erythroblasts with double membranes and spongy heterochromatin

redFlags: Severe anemia refractory to standard treatment
Evidence of iron overload despite no transfusions
references: Iolascon A, et al. Congenital dyserythropoietic anemias: molecular insights and diagnostic challenges. Haematologica. 2013.
Heimpel H, et al. Congenital dyserythropoietic anemia type III: clinical and hematological features. Blood. 1996.
